items.note: In all three samples the newsletter field gets a pink error border, with a warning-icon line under it ('Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com'). The submit stays an ink lift button. The message is clear and nothing overlaps. One pink action shows per viewport (the hero CTA), and the footer form stays ink.

Dark mirrors light. The input gets a pink error border with a readable caption below, and the submit becomes a paper-filled button on the black ground. The newsletter sits in a raised outlined card (samples 2 and 3) or a ruled section (sample 1). Contrast holds.

In samples 2 and 3 the form stacks into one column, with the error border and icon caption under the input and an ink submit. In sample 1 the hero's coin, star and speech-bubble stickers have drifted up over the pink 'Read the featured post' CTA, which covers most of its label.

The form is replaced by a raised, ink-bordered confirmation card with the hard offset shadow. It has a pink check dot and the line 'Thanks for subscribing. New posts will arrive at reader@example.com'. This matches the toast-and-confirmation recipe, and all three samples are consistent.
The same confirmation card sits on the dark ground with a light outline and the 35%-white hard shadow. The pink check is clearly visible and the message reads well in all three samples.
The confirmation card with its hard shadow and check fits the narrow column in every sample. In sample 1 the drifting hero stickers again sit on top of the pink featured-post CTA and hide its label.

The search field shows the pink halo focus with a clear button, the count reads 'Showing 0 of 6 posts', and an empty panel holds one magnifier sticker, 'No posts match these filters', a hint line and a 'Clear filters' button. Samples 1 and 2 keep the button ink because the hero CTA is pink. Sample 3 makes it pink and turns the hero CTA ghost, so each sample has exactly one pink action.

In dark, the sticker, heading, hint and a paper-filled (samples 1 and 2) or pink (sample 3) 'Clear filters' button stay readable. The input halo is visible. Sample 2's panel has a yellow title strip with ink text, which is legible.

The empty panel stacks below the pill filter strip with a large magnifier sticker, one sentence and a full-size Clear filters button. Nothing is clipped and the next step is obvious in all three samples.

Focus sits on the ink current-page 'Home' pill in the header. The 2px ring is drawn with an offset that follows the pill radius, so it is clearly visible and not a browser default. Samples 1 to 3 are the same.
In dark, the current-page pill is paper-filled and the focus ring shows as a pink outline at an offset, distinct against the black header in all three samples.

On mobile the 'Home' pill shows the offset focus ring and the rest of the page is untouched. In sample 1 the hero stickers sit below the CTA here and don't overlap it, which shows that the overlap in the newsletter states depends on scroll position.

The home drawings are flat stickers with heavy ink outlines: coins with an offset rim ellipse and a single heavy glyph, a star, an arrow, a tag, a speech bubble, a stacked-cards figure and a document. Fills come only from pink, yellow and white, and no two drawings repeat. They read clearly at hero size and are as crisp as the reference's coins.

Samples 1 and 2 show their subject: scattered button shapes sorted by an arrow into a tidy grid, and a board of grouped pill rows. Sample 3 is still the generic two-rectangles-on-an-ellipse figure that was already raised as a minor in rc.5 review 1, so it is not raised again.

All three samples draw the idea directly. A sheet of squiggled lines turns, via an arrow, into a sheet of clean lines, marked with a star, a check coin or a band-blue source page. The outlines are heavy, the fills are token colors, and the drawings read well at figure size.

Only sample 2 has a drawing here: a small pink speech-bubble sticker with an ink outline and two ink lines. It is built to the small-sticker recipe and reads as 'note' at icon size. Samples 1 and 3 draw nothing on this page, which the dense-screen rule allows.

The frames show scroll-bound hero drift: the coin, star, arrow and speech bubble each translate upward at their own speed (sample 1), with smaller shifts in samples 2 and 3. Sample 3 also has the linear tag-wall marquee. There is no bounce, scale or fade, and no loop other than the marquee the spec allows.

findings.summary: On phone width, once the page is scrolled down (newsletter states), the scroll-bound drift moves the hero's coin, star and speech-bubble stickers up over the pink 'Read the featured post' CTA. The coin covers most of the label, so the page's main action becomes unreadable and partly hidden.
findings.promptFix: Drifting or decorative shapes must never cover text or controls at any scroll position or width. Lay them out so their whole travel path (start to end of the drift range) stays in empty hero space or behind the edges, and keep them below text and controls in the stacking order (lower z-index, pointer-events: none). Under breakpoint.md, either shrink and move them to the hero's edges or render them static below the content.
